verdicts.why: Deathlok poses as the brainwashed Bakshi's bodyguard, is presented to List as a HYDRA asset and goes on List's HYDRA raid 'to maintain his undercover mission' until Bakshi betrays him (AoS S2 'The Frenemy of My Enemy'). Undercover service counts under the owner's rules, and he is back with S.H.I.E.L.D. once rescued.

Same file as Mike Peterson: in S2 'The Frenemy of My Enemy' he poses as Bakshi's bodyguard and goes on List's HYDRA raid to keep his undercover mission. Undercover service counts, then he returns to S.H.I.E.L.D.

In AoS S3 ('A Wanted (Inhu)man', 'Devils You Know') Hunter wins the HYDRA fight club, 'having secured his place in Hydra' awaits Kebo's orders and is taken on a HYDRA mission as Ward's 'new recruit' before revealing himself. Undercover service counts; he then returns to S.H.I.E.L.D. before the disavowal already on file.

The Secret Warriors split in AoS S3 'The Team' (Daisy: 'it took so little to split our team apart'; Joey and Yo-Yo leave, Daisy defects to Hive; the wiki lists the team as Dismantled). Lincoln refuses to leave and stays with S.H.I.E.L.D. until his death, so his last stage is S.H.I.E.L.D. This matches Joey's and Yo-Yo's records.

In AoS S6, after killing Isaiah, Enoch wears his skin 'to infiltrate the hunters' and takes part in their ambush on the Lighthouse before turning on them. Undercover service counts. 'The Chronicom Hunters' is already the dataset's name (Sibyl), and the order (Chronicoms, betrayed by Isaiah, Hunters, S.H.I.E.L.D.) fits the episode.

In AoS S6 Izel possesses the recreated Flint and uses his powers to rebuild the Monoliths. That is forced service, and Fitz and Simmons already carry the same 'Izel's Crew' S6 stage for their possession. He then escapes, so left 'Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. S6' is right. His S7 enrollment at the Coulson Academy is left alone because HANDOFF holds student-at-a-school and the Flint record split as open owner questions.

In What If...? S1 ep 9, Carter is already a S.H.I.E.L.D. agent leading STRIKE with Natasha on the Lemurian Star when the Watcher recruits her into the Guardians. So S.H.I.E.L.D. belongs in S1 before the Guardians stage, and the S2 return stage stays.

In What If...? S2 ep 5, Natasha calls the Red Room 'home sweet home' ('I can see my bedroom from here'), and before joining S.H.I.E.L.D. she killed its head. HANDOFF keeps past groups (a villain past even outside a file's titles). 'The Red Room' is the name used on screen and on Steve's file in this world, and the stage is keyed to her first title.

In What If...? S2 ep 1, Saal says 'I don't need Black Order trash telling me how to do my job', and Nebula answers 'Former Black Order. I earned my stars here, same as you.' The name is said on screen in this world, and past groups count. Owner note: HANDOFF says the MCU's Nebula is 'Children of Thanos (never the Black Order)', because the main films never say it. If the owner wants that name everywhere, swap it in.

This matches the owner's ruling (#14: Asgard from the start, leaving at What If...? S2 when she turns on King Thor). She is court merlin and advisor to the Asgardian Royal Family and betrays and restrains her king in ep 17. Keying it to her first title (S2) is right with two stages, and left S2 is right.

This matches the owner's ruling (#15). Sir Nick Fury 'served the Asgardian Royal Family as a knight' and betrays his king by stealing the Scepter in ep 17. Asgard S2, then Independent S2 with left S2.

This matches the owner's ruling (#192: 'Young Charles: add the departure at Dark Phoenix (he retires)'). He steps down as dean, the school is renamed and he lives in Paris. The Deadpool 2 glimpse has no story move, and the DOFP closed school stays per ruling #21.

Confirmed on screen: Pierce tells Caliban 'you used to work for my team. You were helping [hunt] those mutants.' Past groups count, and Transigen is the record's own name for Pierce's outfit. But '(from the start)' is only for a single-group file, so the first stage is keyed to his first title, 'Logan'. Left 'Logan' already covers it.

Confirmed on screen: 'So what were special forces doing in Jacksonville?' 'That's classified', and Ajax says 'A dishonorable discharge?' The past group counts and the name is said plainly. But '(from the start)' is only for a single-group file, so the stage is keyed to 'Deadpool'. The discharge is a departure, so also add 'Deadpool' to left.

TAS 'No Mutant Is an Island' (ep 34): Scott strips off his uniform, throws it at Xavier's feet, goes to the orphanage and at the end 'returns to the X-Men'. That is an on-screen quit and return, and left 'X-Men: The Animated Series' is right.

Both quits hold up: in 'Cold Vengeance' he 'decides to leave the X-Men' and 'must return to the X-Men', and in 'Lotus and the Steel' he 'quits the X-Men' and returns with Jubilee. The owner ruled these in ('add his on-screen quit and return... and any other episode where he says he quits'), and left 'X-Men: The Animated Series' is right. Drop the Weapon X stage: the covert squad Weapon X ran is the record's existing Team X stage (the earlier pass filed it as 'Team X/Weapon X'), and the screen calls the four 'former test subjects', so a second stage would count it twice. Unsure, so keep what's there.

In X-Men '97 S1 ep 5, Magneto takes the chancellorship on condition Rogue sits on Genosha's council, and she accepts. Genosha falls in the massacre, and by ep 7 she is back in the field with the X-Men. 'Genosha' is the dataset's name (Magneto and Nightcrawler have the same Genosha, then X-Men pattern in '97 S1).
